doc.title: Classes
doc.para:
Accessing Objects To access member variables, methods, and member properties of a created object, use the . (member selection) operator or [ ] (indirect member selection operator).
var obj=new MyLayer(window,window.prmaryLayer) obj.method1(); // Calling a method; same as obj['method1']() obj.num = 3; // Assignment to a member variable; same as obj['num']=3 obj.prop1++; // Accessing a member property; same as obj['prop1']++

Closures Methods and member properties of a created object are registered with the object along with information about which object's member they belong to. Therefore, even if a method or member property is taken outside the object and used, access will still be made to the original object. This feature is called a closure. Also, the target object being accessed is called the context.
var obj = new FooBarClass(); // Create an object obj.method(); // Ordinarily call the object's method var objmethod = obj.method; // Assign a reference to the object's method to objmethod objmethod(); // Calling objmethod accesses obj, just like obj.method()
The incontextof operator changes the information about which object's member it is, providing a way to execute a method on an arbitrary context.
(objmethod incontextof obj2)(); // Becomes an operation on obj2 (objmethod incontextof this)(); // Becomes an operation on this
